React's default behavior is to re-render all children whenever the parent re-renders, *regardless* of whether their props changed — "same props" doesn't automatically skip the render. The equality check only happens if you explicitly ask for it. A few common culprits: **1. No memoization on the child** By default, a function component re-renders whenever its parent does. Wrap it in `React.memo`: ```jsx const Child = React.memo(function Child({ data }) { return
{data}
; }); ``` `React.memo` does a shallow comparison of props and skips the re-render if they're all `===` equal. **2. Props that *look* the same but aren't (`===` fails)** Even with `React.memo`, this defeats it: ```jsx // new object every render // new array every render doThing()} /> // new function every render ``` Each render creates a brand-new object/array/function, so shallow equality fails even though the *contents* are identical. Fix with `useMemo`/`useCallback` in the parent: ```jsx const options = useMemo(() => ({ foo: 'bar' }), []); const handleClick = useCallback(() => doThing(), []); ``` **3. Context consumers** If the child reads from `useContext`, it re-renders whenever that context value changes — independent of props — including when the provider passes a new object literal as the value. **4. Children as props (JSX)** ```jsx ``` `` here is re-created as a new element object every time `Parent` renders unless `Parent` itself is memoized or the JSX is hoisted/passed down as a stable prop. **Quick way to confirm which one it is:** use `why-did-you-render` or just log prop identities: ```jsx console.log(prevProps.data === nextProps.data); ``` If you paste the parent/child code, I can point to the exact prop that's getting a new reference each time.
